designing data intensive applications is a broad topic
assume the reader already has access to the book 
however, it is difficult to juggle two screens or two apps at once
still it is unwise and unnecessary to copy the entire text 
instead try to find connections to today's context 
and then spend all your energy producing a comprehensive companion 
by which I mean follow the chapters and sub chapters hierarchy 
and include as many quiz questions as possible for each chapter and sub chapter
so learners can test themselves on the knowledge of the book 
focusing on questions that test reasoning and not just recall 
this will be a massive exercise 
where appropriate please also add other questions that exercise foundational knowledge the book assumes readers already possess
please do your best 
do NOT hallucinate 
Please cite the exact text fragment from the book in the answer hint where possible 
Use your best judgment

if there are a lot of files that need to change

    do not include any file that has not changed 
    Any files to delete on updates called out explicitly

The Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2nd edition) companion is done: 1,144 quiz questions across 14 chapters, in one archive, terlingua-ddia-companion.tar.gz. I couldn’t run the repo’s content processor because the .NET SDK wouldn’t download here, so I checked the files against its rules in a separate script.

Structure. The folders follow the book’s chapters. Each chapter starts with a 01-foundations-check section covering background the book assumes (SQL, TCP, percentiles, hashing, base rates and so on), then one section per top-level book section. The preface is included in Chapter 1. Every section has learning objectives, a short summary, and a “Connections to today” list (pgvector and RAG, Iceberg catalogs, the CrowdStrike outage, UUIDv7, Kafka KRaft, Temporal, the EU AI Act, and others). Most questions ask you to reason through a scenario rather than recall a fact.

Quotes. Every explanation outside the foundations checks quotes the book inside “ ”. A script checked all 1,285 quoted fragments against the PDF text and found 0 mismatches. The foundations-check questions are my own and carry no quotes. Where a quote crosses a page break or skips words, I marked the gap with “…”.

Checks against the compiler rules. IDs are valid and unique, every question has at least two options and one correct answer, multi-answer questions are marked type: multiple, and file and folder names follow the numbering pattern. The correct option’s position is spread evenly across A–D.

One weakness: in about 92% of single-answer questions, the correct option is the longest one, so a test-savvy reader could guess. Fixing it means rewriting distractors by hand. I can do that as a follow-up pass, one chapter at a time.

Archive contents (paths relative to the repo root):

content/books/designing-data-intensive-applications/ (new folder: book.yml, 14 chapter folders, 72 sections)
README.md (full file, with a new row in the Library table and one new content-guideline bullet about foundations-check sections)
There are no files to delete.

The Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2nd edition) companion is done: **1,144 quiz questions across 14 chapters**, in one archive, `terlingua-ddia-companion.tar.gz`. I couldn't run the repo's content processor because the .NET SDK wouldn't download here, so I checked the files against its rules in a separate script.

**Structure.** The folders follow the book's chapters. Each chapter starts with a `01-foundations-check` section covering background the book assumes (SQL, TCP, percentiles, hashing, base rates and so on), then one section per top-level book section. The preface is included in Chapter 1. Every section has learning objectives, a short summary, and a "Connections to today" list (pgvector and RAG, Iceberg catalogs, the CrowdStrike outage, UUIDv7, Kafka KRaft, Temporal, the EU AI Act, and others). Most questions ask you to reason through a scenario rather than recall a fact.

**Quotes.** Every explanation outside the foundations checks quotes the book inside “ ”. A script checked all 1,285 quoted fragments against the PDF text and found 0 mismatches. The foundations-check questions are my own and carry no quotes. Where a quote crosses a page break or skips words, I marked the gap with "…".

**Checks against the compiler rules.** IDs are valid and unique, every question has at least two options and one correct answer, multi-answer questions are marked `type: multiple`, and file and folder names follow the numbering pattern. The correct option's position is spread evenly across A–D.

**One weakness:** in about 92% of single-answer questions, the correct option is the longest one, so a test-savvy reader could guess. Fixing it means rewriting distractors by hand. I can do that as a follow-up pass, one chapter at a time.

**Archive contents** (paths relative to the repo root):
- `content/books/designing-data-intensive-applications/` (new folder: `book.yml`, 14 chapter folders, 72 sections)
- `README.md` (full file, with a new row in the Library table and one new content-guideline bullet about foundations-check sections)

There are no files to delete.
